categories.main_business_segments: Kojima Co., Ltd. operates primarily in the retail sector, focusing on the sale of consumer electronics and related products. Its business is structured as a single segment: goods sales, which includes audio-visual products, home appliances, information and communication devices, and other items such as games, toys, and home installation services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced retail management systems, including POS (point-of-sale) systems and electronic shelf labels, to enhance operational efficiency. It emphasizes customer service excellence through structured employee training programs and utilizes digital platforms for e-commerce integration. Energy-saving initiatives, such as LED lighting and solar power installations, are also part of its operational methods.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Kojima serves a broad consumer base, primarily individual customers seeking home electronics, appliances, and related services. It also targets corporate clients through its B2B (corporate sales) and home installation (housing equipment) businesses, and has a growing presence in e-commerce for both individual and business customers.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in Japan, with a network of 139 stores as of August 2025, spanning from Hokkaido in the north to Okinawa in the south. All sales and assets are concentrated within Japan, with no significant overseas operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kojima functions as a downstream player in the supply chain, acting as a retailer that procures products from manufacturers and wholesalers and sells them directly to end consumers and corporate clients. It also collaborates closely with its parent company, Bic Camera, for procurement and logistics.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening store brand power, improving labor productivity, expanding growth businesses (e-commerce, corporate sales, and housing equipment), and enhancing capital efficiency. The company is also focused on sustainability, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions, promoting diversity and employee engagement, and investing in digital transformation and customer experience. There is no significant in-house R&D for product development, as the company is a retailer.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through direct sales of consumer electronics and related products in physical stores and online. Additional income streams include installation services, extended warranties, and a loyalty points program. The company also receives rebates from suppliers based on purchase volumes.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Kojima competes with other major Japanese electronics retailers such as Yamada Denki, Yodobashi Camera, and its parent company Bic Camera. It positions itself as a community-focused, customer-friendly retailer with strong regional presence and service quality, leveraging synergies with Bic Camera for procurement and logistics.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending August 2025, Kojima reported net sales of 282.8 billion yen and net income of 4.7 billion yen, with steady growth in both revenue and profit compared to the previous year. The company maintains a solid financial base with an equity ratio of 58% and continues to invest in store renovations and digital infrastructure.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kojima differentiates itself through high-quality customer service, comprehensive product offerings, and a strong focus on community engagement and sustainability. Its value proposition includes convenient store locations, integrated online and offline shopping experiences, and added-value services such as installation, after-sales support, and loyalty programs.
